title_en: Liang Jieshu v. Nanjing Yuefu Catering Management Co., Ltd. — labor dispute
ruling_gist_en: Workers suffering from special diseases that are difficult to treat, such as cancer or mental illness, shall be entitled to a 24-month medical treatment period. If the labor contract expires during the medical treatment period, the contract shall be extended until the end of the medical treatment period. If the employer unlawfully rescinds or terminates the labor contract during the medical treatment period, and the worker files a lawsuit demanding continued performance of the labor contract, the people's court shall rule to revoke the employer's notice of rescission or termination.

full_text_en:
Liang Jieshu v. Nanjing Yuefu

Catering Management Co., Ltd. — labor dispute

【Ruling Summary】

Workers suffering from special diseases that are difficult to treat, such as cancer or mental illness, shall be entitled to a 24-month medical treatment period. If the labor contract expires during the medical treatment period, the contract shall be extended until the end of the medical treatment period. Where the employer unlawfully terminates or dissolves the labor contract during the medical treatment period, and the worker sues for continued performance of the labor contract, the people's court shall rule to revoke the employer's notice of termination or dissolution.

Plaintiff: Liang Jieshu, male, 19 years old, residing in Xisha Village, Tongyu Town, Binhai County, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Nanjing Yuefu Catering Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Laiyinda Road, Jiangning District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Jingchun, Chairman of the Company.

Plaintiff Liang Jieshu filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing against defendant Nanjing Yuefu Catering Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuefu Catering Company) over a labor dispute.

Plaintiff Liang Jieshu alleged: On November 18, 2009, the plaintiff began working for defendant Yuefu Catering Company as a catering service worker. Subsequently, both parties signed a labor contract with a term from December 1, 2009 to November 30, 2011. The labor contract was kept by the defendant. Due to long daily working hours at the defendant's premises and overwork, the plaintiff suddenly fell ill in early May 2010 and was diagnosed at the hospital with nephrotic syndrome — podocyte disease (uremia). On March 7, 2011, the defendant unilaterally changed the termination date of the labor contract to November 30, 2010, and terminated the labor contract on the grounds that the medical treatment period had expired. The plaintiff's illness should be considered a serious illness, and he should be entitled to a 24-month medical treatment period under the law. The defendant's termination of the labor contract during the medical treatment period was improper. The plaintiff now brings this lawsuit to the court, requesting: 1. Revocation of the notice of termination of labor contract issued by the defendant on March 7, 2011, and maintenance of the labor contract relationship with the defendant; 2. Payment by the defendant of sick leave allowance of RMB 8,208 for March to November 2011 (RMB 1,140/month × 9 months × 80%) and medical treatment period wages of RMB 27,360 (RMB 1,140/month × 24 months), totaling RMB 35,568.

Defendant Yuefu Catering Company argued: The term of the labor contract signed by both parties was from December 1, 2009 to November 30, 2010. Our company did not alter the termination date of the labor contract. Plaintiff Liang Jieshu did not provide evidence that his illness was as severe as major diseases such as paralysis, cancer, or mental illness, and therefore he should not be entitled to a 24-month medical treatment period. Based on the plaintiff's length of service, he should lawfully be entitled to a 3-month medical treatment period. Therefore, terminating the labor contract with the plaintiff on March 7, 2011 was lawful and should not be revoked. We request the court to render a fair judgment in accordance with the law.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing found at first instance:

Plaintiff Liang Jieshu began working for defendant Yuefu Catering Company on November 18, 2009, and both parties signed a labor contract. Liang Jieshu fell ill in early May 2010 and was diagnosed at Nanjing General Hospital of Nanjing Military Command with podocyte disease. He subsequently remained on sick leave, and Yuefu Catering Company paid him sick leave wages through February 2011. On March 7, 2011, Yuefu Catering Company notified Liang Jieshu of the termination of their labor contract relationship on the grounds that it had already extended the contract term to the end of the medical treatment period. On June 7, 2011, Liang Jieshu applied for arbitration with the Nanjing Jiangning District Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Jiangning District Arbitration Committee). On July 11, 2011, the Jiangning District Arbitration Committee issued Arbitration Award No. Ningning Laozhong An Zi (2011) No. 1247. Liang Jieshu, dissatisfied with the award, filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing within the statutory period.

It was also found that the podocyte disease suffered by plaintiff Liang Jieshu is a type of nephrotic syndrome, specifically a kidney podocyte lesion. Uremia is the fourth stage (i.e., the final stage) of chronic renal insufficiency (also known as chronic renal failure), and chronic renal insufficiency is the ultimate outcome of various progressive kidney diseases. Podocyte disease is one of the causes of chronic renal insufficiency. In November 2011, Liang Jieshu was hospitalized at Nanjing General Hospital of Nanjing Military Command due to a relapse of his condition, and the hospital issued a critical illness notice for Liang Jieshu. During treatment, the medical records repeatedly noted that Liang Jieshu's condition was severe and that he was at risk of sudden death at any time, endangering his life.

It was further found that from February 2011, the minimum wage standard in Nanjing was RMB 1,140 per month.

During the trial, defendant Yuefu Catering Company was unable to provide the original signed labor contract and also failed to provide evidence that plaintiff Liang Jieshu held the original contract. In the copy of the labor contract provided by Yuefu Catering Company, the term of the contract was stated as December 1, 2009 to November 30, 2010, with traces of alteration at the "2010" entry. Additionally, Yuefu Catering Company provided an employment registration roster and employee employment registration form filed with the Jiangning District Labor Employment Management Center on October 22, 2010. The employment registration roster and employee registration form recorded Liang Jieshu's labor contract term as December 1, 2009 to November 30, 2010.

The issue in dispute at first instance was: the length of the medical treatment period to which plaintiff Liang Jieshu was entitled.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing held at first instance:

Where a worker falls ill or suffers a non-work-related injury, and the labor contract expires during the statutory medical treatment period, the contract shall be extended until the end of the medical treatment period. Regarding the issue of the medical treatment period to which plaintiff Liang Jieshu was entitled, because his illness was severe, difficult to treat, and posed a risk to life at any time, it should be considered a special disease not subject to the limitation of actual working years. Therefore, Liang Jieshu was entitled to a 24-month medical treatment period. Regarding the termination date of the labor contract signed by both parties, since Yuefu Catering Company failed to provide the original contract, the copy provided showed traces of alteration at the "2010" entry for the termination date, and the filing date of the employment registration roster and employee registration form was after Liang Jieshu fell ill, the court did not accept Yuefu Catering Company's assertion that the contract term expired on November 30, 2010, and accepted Liang Jieshu's assertion that the termination date was November 30, 2011. The labor contract between Liang Jieshu and Yuefu Catering Company expired on November 30, 2011, but this date fell within Liang Jieshu's medical treatment period, so the contract should be extended until the end of the medical treatment period. Defendant Yuefu Catering Company's termination of the labor contract with Liang Jieshu during the medical treatment period violated legal provisions. Therefore, the notice of termination of labor contract issued by Yuefu Catering Company on March 7, 2011 was invalid and should be revoked. Where a worker stops working due to illness or non-work-related injury and is within the statutory medical treatment period, the employer shall pay sick leave wages in accordance with the wage distribution system, at a rate not lower than 80% of the local minimum wage standard. The plaintiff's other claims lacked a basis and were not supported by the court.

In conclusion, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, in accordance with Article 77 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 42 and 45 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 27 and 32 of the Jiangsu Province Wage Payment Regulations, and Article 64(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on November 30, 2011, ruled:

1. Revoke the "Notice of Termination of Labor Contract" issued by defendant Yuefu Catering Company on March 7, 2011.

2. Defendant Yuefu Catering Company shall pay plaintiff Liang Jieshu sick leave wages of RMB 8,208 for the period from March 1, 2011 to November 30, 2011, on the date this judgment takes legal effect.

3. Defendant Yuefu Catering Company shall pay plaintiff Liang Jieshu sick leave wages at 80% of the monthly minimum wage standard of Nanjing each month from the date this judgment takes legal effect until the labor relationship between the parties is lawfully dissolved or terminated.

4. Dismiss the other claims of plaintiff Liang Jieshu.

Yuefu Catering Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, arguing: First, the first-instance trial procedure was improper. During the labor arbitration hearing and before the conclusion of the court debate in the summary procedure applied by the first-instance court, Liang Jieshu had consistently acknowledged the "Notice of Termination of Labor Contract" issued by our company. When the first-instance court applied the ordinary procedure to hear this case, Liang Jieshu changed his claims, asserting that the termination was improper and seeking to maintain the labor relationship, which clearly exceeded the statutory time limit. Second, the first-instance judgment's revocation of the "Notice of Termination of Labor Contract" was erroneous. During the hearing of the labor dispute case No. Ningning Laozhong An Zi (2010) No. 2265 before the Nanjing Jiangning District Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee, Liang Jieshu raised no objection to our company's presentation of the labor contract with a termination date of "November 30, 2010." Pursuant to Article 9(5) of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, facts confirmed by an effective arbitration award do not require proof by the parties, and therefore our company is not required to provide the original labor contract. Liang Jieshu's current condition does not constitute uremia; he should be entitled to a 3-month medical treatment period, not 24 months. Our company's termination of the labor contract in March 2011 was lawful. We request the appellate court to set aside the first-instance judgment and instead rule that our company shall pay Liang Jieshu economic compensation for termination of the labor contract and sick leave wages for March 2011.

The appellee Liang Jieshu argued: The first-instance court correctly found the facts and correctly applied the law. We request the appellate court to rule in accordance with the law.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, upon second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

It was further found at second instance that the requests made by appellee Liang Jieshu during the arbitration stage were: appellant Yuefu Catering Company pay economic compensation for termination of the labor contract of RMB 2,280; sick leave allowance of RMB 8,208 for March to November 2011; medical treatment period wages of RMB 6,840; medical subsidy of RMB 20,520; make social insurance contributions through November 2011; and handle procedures for transfer of personnel file and social insurance relationship. On August 10, 2011, Liang Jieshu submitted a complaint to the first-instance court with the following claims: 1. Due to the improper termination of the labor relationship, Yuefu Catering Company shall pay a total of RMB 37,848, including economic compensation for termination of the contract of RMB 2,280, sick leave allowance of RMB 8,208 for March to November 2011, and medical treatment period wages of RMB 20,520; 2. Yuefu Catering Company shall make social insurance contributions for Liang Jieshu through November 2011; 3. Yuefu Catering Company shall handle the transfer of his personnel file and social insurance relationship. On September 6, 2011, the first-instance court held the first hearing under the summary procedure, and Liang Jieshu changed the claim for medical treatment period wages to RMB 27,360, with other claims as in the complaint. On November 6, 2011, the first-instance court converted the case from summary procedure to ordinary procedure. On November 15, 2011, Liang Jieshu submitted a written change of claims to the first-instance court, requesting: a ruling that Yuefu Catering Company's termination of the labor relationship was improper and that the labor relationship be maintained; and waiving the claim for economic compensation for termination of the contract of RMB 2,280. Other claims remained unchanged. On November 22, 2011, the first-instance court held a hearing under the ordinary procedure (Yuefu Catering Company waived the evidence submission period), and Liang Jieshu stated in court that he waived the request for handling the transfer of personnel file and social insurance relationship. The Nanjing Jiangning District Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee's Arbitration Award No. Ningning Laozhong An Zi (2010) No. 2265, issued on November 3, 2010, did not confirm that the term of the labor contract between Liang Jieshu and Yuefu Catering Company was from December 1, 2009 to November 30, 2010.

The issue in dispute at second instance remained: the length of the medical treatment period to which appellee Liang Jieshu was entitled.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

Appellee Liang Jieshu's change of claims before the conclusion of the court debate complied with Article 156 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The first-instance court's trial and judgment based on Liang Jieshu's final clarified claims were procedurally proper. Regarding the issue of the expiration date of the labor contract. Both Liang Jieshu and appellant Yuefu Catering Company acknowledged that a labor contract was signed. Yuefu Catering Company failed to provide the original labor contract. The copy it provided stated that the contract was signed on November 18, 2009, with a term from December 1, 2009 to November 30, 2010, and there were traces of alteration at the second "0" in "2010." On October 22, 2010, Yuefu Catering Company filed this labor contract with the Nanjing Jiangning District Labor Employment Management Center for record. Liang Jieshu argued that the expiration date of the labor contract was November 30, 2011; Yuefu Catering Company argued that it was November 30, 2010. Given that Yuefu Catering Company failed to provide the original labor contract, the content regarding the term in the copy showed alterations, and the date of contract filing was after Liang Jieshu fell ill and near the expiration date of the contract term as claimed by Yuefu Catering Company, Yuefu Catering Company's assertion that the expiration date was November 30, 2010 lacked sufficient evidence. The appellant's claim that the Nanjing Jiangning District Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee's Arbitration Award No. Ningning Laozhong An Zi (2010) No. 2265 confirmed the contract term as December 1, 2009 to November 30, 2010 was factually unfounded. Regarding the issue of the medical treatment period. The first-instance court, based on Liang Jieshu's condition, found that his illness was severe and constituted a special disease, entitling him to a 24-month medical treatment period. This was consistent with the content of the former Ministry of Labor's Notice on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Provisions on Medical Treatment Periods for Enterprise Workers Who Are Ill or Non-Work-Related Injured (Lao Bu Fa [1995] No. 236). Liang Jieshu's illness fell within the statutory medical treatment period, and the term of the labor contract should be automatically extended until the end of the medical treatment period. Yuefu Catering Company's notification to Liang Jieshu on March 7, 2011 terminating the labor contract violated Article 45 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China.

In conclusion, the appellant Yuefu Catering Company's appeal lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and the disposition was proper. Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on February 20, 2012, ruled:

Reject the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

This judgment is final.
